resource.name: aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule
resource.description: Manages an inbound (ingress) rule for a security group. When specifying an inbound rule for your security group in a VPC, the configuration must include a source for the traffic. Using aws_vpc_security_group_egress_rule and aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule resources is the current best practice. Avoid using the aws_security_group_rule resource and the ingress and egress arguments of the aws_security_group resource for configuring in-line rules, as they struggle with managing multiple CIDR blocks, and tags and descriptions due to the historical lack of unique IDs. You should not use the aws_vpc_security_group_egress_rule and aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule resources in conjunction with the aws_security_group resource with in-line rules (using the ingress and egress arguments of aws_security_group) or the aws_security_group_rule resource. Doing so may cause rule conflicts, perpetual differences, and result in rules being overwritten.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule` resource enables precise management of inbound traffic rules for AWS VPC security groups, ensuring granular control over allowed sources such as IP ranges, CIDR blocks, or other security groups. It is commonly used to configure secure access for applications, services, or databases by defining specific protocols, ports, and trusted traffic origins. This resource is ideal for scenarios requiring scalable rule management, support for multiple CIDR blocks, and enhanced tagging and descriptions, avoiding conflicts and limitations associated with in-line rules or legacy configurations.

examples.title: Basic Usage
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an ingress rule for an AWS Security Group using the `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule` resource. It shows how to allow TCP traffic on port 80 from a specified IPv4 CIDR block (`10.0.0.0/8`) by associating the rule with a Security Group created in a specific VPC.

arguments.name: cidr_ipv4
arguments.llm_summary: The `cidr_ipv4` argument in the `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule` resource allows users to specify the IPv4 CIDR range that defines the source of incoming traffic permitted by the security group rule. By setting this argument, users can control access to their resources by restricting or allowing traffic from specific IPv4 address ranges, supporting common security goals like limiting exposure to trusted networks or external systems.

arguments.name: cidr_ipv6
arguments.llm_summary: The `cidr_ipv6` argument in the `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule` resource allows users to specify an IPv6 CIDR range as the source for incoming traffic rules. By setting this argument, users can define which IPv6 addresses are permitted to access resources within the VPC, enabling fine-grained control over ingress traffic for IPv6-based networks.

arguments.name: description
arguments.llm_summary: The `description` argument for the `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule` resource allows users to specify a human-readable explanation or label for the ingress rule, providing context or documentation about its purpose, such as identifying the rule's intent or associated application. Setting this argument enhances clarity and maintainability, especially in environments with multiple rules, by enabling users to track and understand the rule's function within the security group configuration.

arguments.name: from_port
arguments.description: (Optional) The start of port range for the TCP and UDP protocols, or an ICMP/ICMPv6 type.
arguments.llm_summary: The `from_port` argument in the `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule` resource allows users to define the starting port of a range for TCP, UDP, or ICMP/ICMPv6 traffic. By specifying this value, users control which inbound traffic is permitted based on the protocol and port range, enabling fine-grained access control for their VPC security group.

arguments.name: ip_protocol
arguments.description: (Required) The IP protocol name or number. Use `-1` to specify all protocols. Note that if `ip_protocol` is set to `-1`, it translates to all protocols, all port ranges, and `from_port` and `to_port` values should not be defined.
arguments.llm_summary: The `ip_protocol` argument in the `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule` resource specifies the network protocol (e.g., TCP, UDP, ICMP) or protocol number for the ingress rule, enabling users to control which types of traffic are allowed into the associated security group. Setting this argument to `-1` allows all protocols and port ranges, providing broad access, while defining a specific protocol restricts traffic to that protocol type, aligning with common security and access control goals.

arguments.name: prefix_list_id
arguments.description: (Optional) The ID of the source prefix list.
arguments.llm_summary: The `prefix_list_id` argument allows users to specify the ID of an AWS-managed or customer-managed prefix list as a source for the security group ingress rule. This enables the configuration of access control based on predefined sets of IP address ranges, simplifying management and ensuring consistent application of network policies.

arguments.name: referenced_security_group_id
arguments.description: (Optional) The source security group that is referenced in the rule.
arguments.llm_summary: The `referenced_security_group_id` argument in the `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule` resource allows users to specify the ID of a source security group whose members are permitted ingress access based on the rule. By setting this argument, users can define security group-to-security group relationships, enabling controlled access between resources within or across VPCs, which is commonly used for managing inter-service communication or shared access policies.

arguments.name: security_group_id
arguments.description: (Required) The ID of the security group.
arguments.llm_summary: The `security_group_id` argument specifies the ID of the security group to which the ingress rule will be applied, enabling users to define and control inbound traffic permissions for that specific security group. By setting this argument, users associate the ingress rule with a targeted security group, ensuring precise traffic filtering and access control within their VPC environment.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: (Optional) A map of tags to assign to the resource. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags` argument in the `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule` resource allows users to assign metadata in the form of key-value pairs to the ingress rule, enabling resource categorization, organization, and identification for purposes such as cost allocation, environment labeling, or compliance tracking. When configured, these tags can override provider-level default tags, ensuring granular control over resource-specific tagging.

arguments.name: to_port
arguments.description: (Optional) The end of port range for the TCP and UDP protocols, or an ICMP/ICMPv6 code.
arguments.llm_summary: The `to_port` argument in the `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule` resource allows users to define the upper boundary of a port range for TCP and UDP protocols or specify an ICMP/ICMPv6 code. By setting this argument, users can control the scope of allowed network traffic, enabling fine-grained access management for inbound connections to their VPC resources.

attributes.name: arn
attributes.description: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the security group rule.

attributes.name: security_group_rule_id
attributes.description: The ID of the security group rule.

attributes.name: tags_all
attributes.description: A map of tags assigned to the resource, including those inherited from the provider `default_tags` configuration block.
